content.thinking:
I should focus on root cause, executive summary, and assumptions without restating computed impact figures as my own—those belong to the shop. I can reference the given timestamps directly, like the incident spanning roughly 17:39 to 17:45, about six minutes, since that's stated data rather than something I calculated.

For error rates I'll stay qualitative, saying something like "a large share of account page requests failed" rather than inventing or restating specific percentages. My assumptions should note: the flag toggle wasn't paired with a deploy per the single change event recorded; no code change occurred; the ZeroDivisionError traces to the disabled-fallback path; who toggled the flag and why is unknown; recovery correlates with the revert but isn't definitively proven; and the underlying divide-by-zero defect likely still exists behind the flag, per the open draft PR. I'll also note the mitigation was simply re-enabling the fallback flag, while the actual code defect remains unresolved. For the executive summary, I'll keep it general—referring to "the online shop's account page" rather than internal component or flag names.

assumptions: The flag toggle is assumed to be the trigger on the strength of timing and the absence of any other recorded change; no deploy or config push outside the flag system was found in the change history searched (roughly the preceding 42 hours).
Who toggled the flag and why is not recorded in anything reviewed here; it is assumed to have been a deliberate human or automated flag change rather than a flag-provider fault.
The return to baseline after 17:45 is attributed to the flag revert on correlation alone — no independent confirmation that nothing else changed at the same moment.

The underlying divide-by-zero defect is assumed to still be present in the non-fallback code path; the incident was mitigated by avoiding that path, not by fixing it. Re-disabling the flag before the draft PR merges would be expected to reproduce the outage.
The pre-incident ClientDisconnected errors are assumed to be normal background noise unrelated to this fault.
Impact is characterised only for the account page, since that is the only surface named in the logs reviewed; other endpoints were not separately examined.
input.executive_summary: On 26 September 2026 a configuration switch in the online shop was flipped at 17:39 UTC, sending customer traffic down a newer version of the account-page code that contained a latent bug. From that moment, a substantial share of visits to the account page failed outright; the rest of the site's traffic was unaffected. Automated monitoring raised an alert at 17:44, the cause was traced to the switch within about a minute, and the switch was put back to its previous setting at 17:45. The page returned to its normal error levels immediately, and recovery was confirmed at 17:46. The customer-facing disruption ran from 17:39 to 17:45 — roughly six minutes. A draft code fix for the underlying bug has been opened for review; until it merges, the shop is running on the older fallback path.
input.root_cause: The feature flag `legacy-checkout-fallback` was switched from on to off at 17:39, routing account-page traffic onto the newer spend-summary code path, which divides by zero (`ZeroDivisionError` at `src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47`) and failed every request that reached it. No deploy or code change appears in the change history around the onset — the flag toggle is the only recorded change, and it lines up exactly with the start of the errors, so the defect was latent in the non-fallback path and the toggle merely exposed it.
